purpose: Consult before defining a glossary term. If a prior published lesson already defines it, adopt that meaning and cross-reference, or declare a glossary `alignment` block that names the prior lesson and the relation (adopt/narrow/extend/distinct-sense/supersede) with a rationale. Never silently redefine a term another lesson owns.

uses.definition: A statement recorded because the person themself said it. Its check is to ask the person again, and its value depends on whether the person's own wording was kept.
Study that builds knowledge and reasoning through sources, fictional cases, analyses, and simulations without conferring authority to assess or treat real people.

The emotional expression an examiner observed during an encounter: the face, the voice, the posture, and how those moved as the conversation moved. It reaches the record through the examiner's eyes and covers only the period observed. Affect is not evidence of mood and mood is not evidence of affect.

The moment-to-moment expression of emotional state that an observer sees during a bounded stretch of time, including its range and how it moves. In a description it is written as an observation, and its time course is the length of the contact.

alignment.note: Adopted unchanged from the earlier mental-status observation outcome. This lesson uses the distinction for one purpose: mood and affect are separate lines with separate sources, so a later reader can see one move while the other does not.

uses.definition: The state that follows reduction or cessation of alcohol in a person who has become physically dependent on it. Its severe forms include withdrawal seizures and delirium and are life-threatening, which is why the risk is assessed before any planned period of abstinence and why people found to be at risk have their withdrawal medically assisted where assessment and monitoring are available around the clock. This lesson uses the term only to mark the assessment that precedes an abstinence interval; managing withdrawal is outside its scope.

A psychiatric presentation judged to belong to alcohol use rather than to be independent of it, on the grounds that its features appear only during periods of problem drinking and settle during extended sobriety. The judgement is made from chronology, not from the presence of drinking.
Loss of interest in activities and loss of the pleasure they previously gave. It is described separately from low mood because the two can begin at different times and can move separately.

A statement recorded because an informant, someone who knows the person and is speaking about them, said it. Its check is to ask that informant, and its weight depends on which parts of the person's life the informant actually sees.

A course in which one or more episodes of elevated or activated mood have occurred alongside depressive episodes, whether or not any of them reached the threshold for mania. Used here as an alternative on a differential and not as a diagnosis given to anyone.

The ability to make a particular decision at a particular time, meaning the ability to understand the information relevant to that decision and to appreciate what following or refusing it would reasonably mean. Capacity is decision-specific; having a psychiatric condition, disagreeing with a recommendation, or choosing something the clinician thinks unwise does not by itself establish its absence. This lesson names capacity as a condition of the consent model and does not teach how it is assessed.

A statement that one thing is producing or maintaining another. Its check is evidence that separates it from a named rival account, so a causal explanation with no rival named is not being checked at all.

The route by which an item of evidence reached you, together with how far that route can be relied on for that kind of content. A person's memory of a past week, an informant who was there, a contemporaneous record, and prospective observation are four channels of differing strength.

A statement that a picture meets the requirements of a named category in a published set of diagnostic guidelines. Its check is agreement: whether a second clinician applying the same guideline reaches the same category.
Jurisdiction-dependent responsibility and authorisation to perform clinical actions with real people within a regulated professional role; academic knowledge alone does not create it.

alignment.note: PSY-WEL-001 owns this term and this lesson keeps its meaning unchanged. It is repeated here because the role boundary in this lesson is stated in terms of acts and the people they land on, and a learner needs the earlier definition in hand to see that the boundary follows authorisation and supervision rather than the difficulty of the subject matter. The prose links back to the owning lesson at first use.

uses.definition: Jurisdiction-dependent responsibility and authorization to perform clinical actions with real people within a regulated professional role; academic knowledge alone does not create it.

This lesson's first check on a sentence in a mental-status description: does the sentence still hold when you add the words during those forty minutes. A sentence that fails has stopped describing a period of observation and started describing a person.

An account of a person's presentation given by someone else, such as a relative, housemate, employer, or an earlier clinical record. Its value is set by the informant's vantage point: what they were actually in a position to see, and over what period.

An account of a person's history given, with that person's consent, by someone else who was present, or taken from a record written at the time. It is used here as a second channel running alongside the person's own account and never as a substitute for it. An informant can describe how a state looked from outside, which the person cannot, and is bounded by which periods they witnessed, their own recall across the same interval, and their relationship to the person.

The arrangements that make an encounter usable by the person in it: a professional interpreter, a signed-language interpreter, a longer appointment, written summaries, a hearing loop, an easy-read explanation, or a communication partner. It is arranged before the encounter because it cannot be improvised inside it, and an accompanying relative is not one of these arrangements.

The duty to keep what a person discloses within the care of the people who need it for that person's care. It is strong and it is bounded: its limits are fixed by the law and professional regulation of a particular place, so any description of those limits is accurate for one jurisdiction at a time.

Whether the affect observed fits the mood the person has reported and the subject being discussed. Congruence is a judgement, so a description records it alongside the observed events it rests on, which lets a later reader, or the person described, disagree with the reading.

A phrase that shortens a clinical description by discarding the observation behind it and putting a judgement about the person in its place, as poor historian, poorly motivated, and denies do. It is distinguished from ordinary compression, which shortens the writing while leaving the information recoverable.

A word carrying two meanings that get exchanged without notice. In ordinary speech it names a low mood, usually about something and usually passing. In clinical use a major depressive episode names a syndrome requiring depressed mood or loss of interest and pleasure most days for at least two weeks, with several further changes and dysfunction alongside. This lesson writes low mood for the first and spells the syndrome out in full for the second.

In this lesson, the clinical syndrome: a sustained change in mood, interest, sleep, appetite, energy, concentration and function, described over a stated period. The same word is used in ordinary speech for feeling low for an afternoon, and the two senses are kept apart throughout. What the syndrome consists of is described in mood phenomenology and function (PSY-250.01) rather than here.

A statement of what was reported or observed, written so that another clinician who was not present could have written the same words from the same material. A description carries no conclusion about what the findings mean.

alignment.note: The description, inference, and interpretation distinction is owned by the earlier outcome on description and inference, and this lesson keeps that meaning unchanged. What this lesson adds is the practical consequence: a description that has lost its source has stopped being a description, because nobody downstream can reproduce it.

uses.definition: The layer of a record that states what was reported and what was observed, without a conclusion about what any of it means. In this lesson it covers a person's report, another person's report, and direct observation.
The misattribution of a person's physical symptoms to their existing mental illness, so that a physical cause is investigated less than it otherwise would be.

A set of live alternatives for a presentation, each one recorded with what speaks for it, what speaks against it, which parts of it nobody has asked about, and what would close the remainder. Some alternatives can then be ordered against one another and some cannot, and an alternative nobody enquired into is not ordered at all. A list of category names with no evidence attached is not a differential.
A record of what an examiner saw or heard inside one bounded encounter, written so that another person present at the time could have agreed or disagreed. Its check expires when the encounter ends.

alignment.note: PREM-SCI-001 owns observation as a record of what was noticed or measured, stated so that its object, conditions, and result can be checked. That meaning is kept and narrowed to the clinical encounter: the conditions are one bounded stretch of time with named people in the room, which is what makes the check a second person present at the time and what makes it expire.

uses.definition: Waking earlier than intended and not returning to sleep. Described with a time, a frequency, and whether sleep returns, because those three are what allow a later comparison.

One described change within a presentation, such as the sleep, the appetite, or the ability to hold a thought. In this lesson each element is written with three things attached: what changed, its time course, and its source.

Mood raised or expansive beyond the person's usual state, described as part of a distinct period that also carries increased activity or energy. In a description it is dated and sourced like any other element, and naming what kind of episode it belongs to is a separate task.

A finding that a change is absent because the question was put and answered in the negative. It is written down, and it is different from a record that simply says nothing, which leaves a later reader unable to tell absence from an unasked question.
The representation a causal explanation commits its writer to: which features of a situation are selected, which are treated as background, and which way the influence is asserted to run.

alignment.note: PREM-WEL-001 owns model as a purposeful representation of selected features and relationships used to explain, predict, or test within stated limits, and PREM-SCI-010 adopts it. That meaning is kept and narrowed to the small model implied by a single causal sentence in a clinical record, which is usually left unstated and which this lesson asks the writer to say out loud.

uses.definition: Specific things a person did before and now does differently, each with a date and a source, covering work, study, household tasks, self-care, and contact with other people. A single global rating of function is not a description of it.

A period of elevated, expansive or irritable mood with increased energy or activity that is a change from the person's usual state and is noticeable to others, without the severity that marks mania. Its minimum duration is a convention rather than a finding, and this lesson records that the convention is contested.

A conclusion you have drawn from findings, such as calling a person withdrawn, guarded, or minimising. Inferences are legitimate and useful, and they belong in your impression rather than on a line that reports what happened.

alignment.note: Adopted unchanged from the earlier outcome on description and inference. This lesson uses it only to enforce one rule: an inference may not occupy a finding line, because a later reader cannot tell it apart from something that was seen or said.

uses.definition: A conclusion drawn from observations and reasoning rather than something recorded directly. Its check is to display the statements it rests on and see whether they carry it.

alignment.note: PREM-SCI-001 owns this word and its meaning is kept unchanged. One thing does change: that lesson allows interpretation as an alias for inference, and this lesson does not carry the alias forward, because psychiatry needs interpretation to cover classification and causal explanation as well. Inference therefore stays narrow here and the two other kinds keep their own names.

uses.definition: A person's voluntary agreement to something proposed, given with enough information for the choice to mean something, by a person able to make it. It is a continuing arrangement that is reviewed and renewed as circumstances change; a signature or a note records that the discussion happened at a moment and is evidence of the agreement rather than the agreement itself.

In this lesson, the two kinds of statement that go furthest past a description: a classification and a causal explanation. Ordinary usage runs the word together with inference; this lesson keeps them apart because their checks differ.

alignment.note: PREM-SCI-001 lists interpretation as an alias for inference, so in the premed corpus the two words name one thing. Psychiatry needs the word for something else: the classification and the causal explanation, which are conclusions of a different kind and are checked by agreement and by a named rival rather than by displaying their material. The prose bridges the two senses where the word is first reserved, and inference keeps its premed meaning unchanged.

uses.definition: Mood in which small provocations produce anger or impatience out of proportion to the person's usual response. It is the alternative direction the same element can take alongside elevated mood, and on its own it discriminates very little, since it accompanies a wide range of states.

A number summarising how often two independent raters assign the same category, adjusted downwards for the agreement that guessing alone would produce. A kappa of 1 means they always agree and a kappa of 0 means they agree no more often than chance would arrange.
A disciplined level or perspective used to generate a particular kind of question; a lens is not evidence that its proposed explanation is relevant or causal.
Evidence about the shape of a person's illness over time: which episodes occurred, in what order, for how long, what happened between them, and what changed alongside them.

The described state of persistently lowered mood, written as an element with its own onset, duration, pattern, and source. Using this phrase keeps a description from implying the clinical syndrome before anyone has established it.

The part of a psychiatric assessment that describes how a person appeared, spoke, moved, and responded during the evaluation itself. It reports a period of observation with a stated beginning and end; the history carries the longer course.

Depressive and elevated features running inside the same episode. How often this is recorded depends strongly on which criteria are applied, so a description states the co-occurring features and their dates and leaves the labelling to a later step.

The person's own account of their sustained emotional state. It reaches the record through what they say, it covers whatever period they are describing, and it is written in their words wherever they have supplied words. In ordinary speech mood and affect are interchangeable; in a psychiatric description they are not, and this lesson keeps them apart.
The sustained emotional state a person reports from the inside, holding across hours to weeks. In a description it is written from the person's own account, with its own time course.

alignment.note: The mood and affect distinction is owned by the earlier mental-status observation outcome, and this lesson adopts it unchanged. Ordinary speech treats the two words as interchangeable, which is why the worked example names them side by side at the point where a reported state and an observed expression have to go on separate lines.

uses.definition: A person's sustained internal emotional state over a period, as against the moment-to-moment expressed emotion an observer sees during a conversation. This lesson uses mood only in that sustained sense, because its subject is how a state behaves over months and years.

alignment.note: The psychiatry block assigns the mood and affect distinction to mental-status observation (PSY-INT-004), which is not yet authored. This lesson adopts that distinction in advance and uses only the mood side of it, so that the term does not acquire a second sense before its owning lesson exists. If PSY-INT-004 words the distinction differently, this entry follows it.

uses.definition: The set of changes a person brings to a clinical contact, described element by element with what changed, over what period, and where the information came from. A presentation is a description of a person at a time; it is not a diagnosis and does not name one.

A bereavement-related syndrome whose distinguishing features are separation distress and persistent yearning for the person who died. It is descriptively distinct from depression and from post-traumatic stress while co-occurring with them often, so finding one is no reason to stop looking for the others.

Evidence generated by recording what happens from today forward. Writing the question and the meaning of each possible outcome down before the recording starts makes the result easier to interpret and harder to reshape once it is known. An observation nobody planned still contributes when it was recorded as it happened, carrying the extra requirement that the record say what was and was not being watched for. What produces no evidence is an interval with no record at all, which becomes another retrospective account later.

A medical field that studies and responds to patterns of experience, behaviour, bodily process, relationship, culture, and context; this lesson teaches its academic scope, not authority to practise it.

Slowing or agitation in movement, speech, and the speed of responding, described from what an observer saw during a bounded contact. It is recorded separately from what the person reports about energy, because the two have different sources and can move separately.

Delusions or hallucinations occurring within a mood episode. They are called mood-congruent when their content fits the mood state and mood-incongruent when it does not. Their absence counts as a finding only when the question was actually asked.

How much of the available emotional expression appeared during the observed period. The conventional descriptive words run from flat, through blunted and restricted, up to full and broad. A range can only be described over a period long enough for expression to have had a chance to vary.

The state in which every person in an encounter knows who the others are, what each is there to do, and which of them carries responsibility for any decision that follows. It is a property of what was said out loud, not of what happened to be true, which is why an unintroduced observer leaves the encounter without it.
The lesson's four-question procedure for checking who is affected, what action is proposed, what could happen if it is wrong, and which governed route the action requires.

The arranged conditions of an encounter: the place, the people present, the time available, the way information will be recorded and shared, and what each person is there to do. The setting is chosen, so it can be chosen differently, and it constrains what a person is able to say.
A designed practice setting using a fictional scenario, standardized participant, model, or supplied data so a learner can rehearse reasoning without representing the activity as real-patient care.
Where an element came from, which in this lesson is exactly one of three things: the person's own report, another person's report or record, or your own observation. Inference is not a source.

This lesson's second check on a sentence in a mental-status description: could a reader who was not present say what happened in the room from this sentence alone. A sentence that fails has replaced an observation with the writer's conclusion about it.

A thyroid result pattern of raised thyroid-stimulating hormone with a free thyroxine still inside the reference range. It is a common incidental finding when depressed people are tested, and it is not established to cause or worsen depression.
The four temporal facts an element needs: when it began and how sharply, how long it has run, what pattern it follows within a day or a week, and whether it is worsening, steady, or easing.

An alternative nobody has enquired into, so the record holds nothing for it and nothing against it. It has no position on a differential at all, and placing it low reports the result of a search that was never run. Whether an alternative was asked about is a separate reading from what the evidence says about it, and an alternative can be partly assessed: supported and countered on the questions that were put, and silent on the ones that were not.

A course of one or more depressive episodes in which no episode of elevated or activated mood has occurred. It is defined by an absence, which is why it can only ever be as secure as the search for that absence has been.

The condition of an agreement being free of the pressures that limit or control a choice, such as institutional constraint, fear, coercion, undue influence, or misrepresentation. Voluntariness is a property of the circumstances in which the answer was given and not of the answer itself, so a yes given under pressure carries little information.

Of an item of evidence in this lesson: how far it would move the ranking of alternatives if it happened exactly as described. Weight is a property of the content and can be judged before you know whether the item is true.
